clue.text: Second warning in case of misconduct

indicators.note: in tells us the warning word sits inside the letters that follow it
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A teacher issues a second warning to a pupil caught misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment and a second are both very short spans of time: 'wait a second' is 'wait a moment'.

clue.text: Male journalist welcoming a go-between

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest in, so the journalist word holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: an editor is a senior journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaperman takes in someone who arbitrates between parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mediator acts as an intermediary between two sides in a dispute.

clue.text: Excuse to kiss TS Eliot cheekily seized by setter

indicators.note: seized by means held within the grip of the setter word, which goes round the rest

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: cheekily suggests impudent play, so the poet's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter grabs the poet T S Eliot and plants a cheeky kiss on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excuse to kiss' is a playful definition rather than a synonym; 'cheekily' is the anagram signal on the poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas custom: standing under a sprig of the plant hung indoors licenses a kiss, so it is a pretext for one.

clue.text: Pinch bottoms of Bishan Bedi and Dominic Cork

indicators.note: in a down answer the bottom of each word is its last letter, so take the last letter of each

explanation.surface: Two cricketers, the Indian spinner Bishan Bedi and the English all-rounder Dominic Cork, get their backsides pinched.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: to pinch something is to steal it, and in British slang to nick it.

clue.text: Calamity of girl with bloomers back to front

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: back to front tells us the last letter of the flower word is moved to the front

parts.note: bloomers here are flowers, and asters are flowers

explanation.surface: A girl's undergarments put on back to front make for an embarrassing calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like knickers but means flowers; 'back to front' moves the final S of ASTERS to the start, giving SASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a calamity is a terrible misfortune or catastrophe.

clue.text: Laundering this amount of money over in Panama?

indicators.note: laundering money is cleaning it up, here churning the letters of the little word
over means turned over, so the money word is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: Money laundering in Panama, the notorious tax haven, is hinted at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laundering' rearranges THIS to ISTH; 'over' reverses SUM to MUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Example, signalled by the question mark: Panama is the classic narrow land bridge joining two continents.

clue.text: Lovely piece of writing in review of musical

indicators.note: in places the piece of writing inside the reversed show title
review is read as re-view, looking back, so the musical's name runs backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
a tract is a short written treatise

explanation.surface: A critic praises a lovely bit of prose in a review of a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' looks like a critic's write-up, but read as re-view it means looking backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something lovely is pleasing to look at, appealing.

clue.text: Punch end of recalcitrant camel's protruberance

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a camel's hump is the lump on its back

explanation.surface: Someone punches the end of a stubborn camel's hump.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to punch someone is to hit them hard, to wallop them.

clue.text: I'm afraid boring communist stank

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the cry of fright goes into the communist word

parts.note: a Red is a communist
eek is the cry of someone frightened

explanation.surface: I'm afraid the dull communist smelled bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull but means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to stink or smell strongly and unpleasantly, past tense.

clue.text: Be merciful to average fellow

parts.note: par is the average or standard level
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: An instruction to go easy on an ordinary bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to forgive or excuse an offender is to show them mercy.

clue.text: Accidents in tumble drier

indicators.note: in tumble means tossed about, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mishaps happen inside a tumble drier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumble drier' looks like one appliance; 'in tumble' is the anagram signal and 'drier' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a desiccant is a drying agent such as silica gel, which absorbs moisture.

clue.text: Finally capitulate after rejecting short ceasefire

indicators.note: after puts the final letter behind the reversed piece
rejecting means turning back, so the word for short runs backwards

parts.note: curt means short or brusque

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A side finally gives in after turning down a brief ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short ceasefire' looks like one phrase; 'short' belongs to the wordplay and 'ceasefire' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a truce is an agreed halt to fighting.

clue.text: Friend of much pilloried aunt scratching head

indicators.note: scratching head means scraping off the first letter

parts.note: an Aunt Sally is a fairground target for thrown objects, hence anyone much criticised

explanation.surface: A pal of a much-mocked aunt is scratching their head.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British fairground game of throwing sticks at a dummy's head, hence a target of abuse; 'scratching head' drops the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an ally is a friend or supporter on your side.

clue.text: Papa's medal could produce a lump in the throat

indicators.note: could produce suggests making something new from the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seeing father's medal might make one tearfully emotional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lump in the throat' looks like the emotion, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal reading: the Adam's apple is the visible bulge of the larynx at the front of the neck.

clue.text: Daring kiss, source of congestion

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or daring
to neck is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: A bold kiss, oddly said to cause a traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, having bottle means having courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a narrow point in a road where traffic piles up is a classic cause of jams.

clue.text: Antiquated old couple drowned in vat of tea?

indicators.note: drowned in means submerged inside the container word

parts.note: an urn is a large vessel for making tea
a couple is two

explanation.surface: An elderly pair have drowned in a vat of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: outdated, out of fashion, no longer of use.

clue.text: On vacation, surprise mates with arrangements

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outer letters of the next word stay

parts.note: a ram tups a ewe: to tup is to mate

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers spring a surprise on their friends with plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mates' looks like friends but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: set-ups are arrangements or organisational structures.

clue.text: Quietly wax lyrical about oligarch's principal residence

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly

indicators.note: about means going round, so the enthusing word goes round the oligarch's first letter

parts.note: to wax lyrical is to gush with enthusiasm

indicators.note: principal means first, so take the opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone gushes softly about a Russian tycoon's main home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal residence' looks like one phrase; 'principal' gives O and 'residence' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a luxury flat on the top floor of a building is a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Great success of mum's two husbands described by brood

indicators.note: described by means drawn round, so the brooding word encircles the rest

parts.note: a hen broods or sits on its eggs
ma is mum, so mum's gives ma's
H is the abbreviation for husband, twice

explanation.surface: Mum's two marriages are recounted by her children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brood' looks like offspring but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a smash hit is a show or record that is a huge popular success.

clue.text: Infected by bacteria, Mick sheds skin after 30 days

indicators.note: after places the trimmed name behind the month

parts.note: September has thirty days, abbreviated Sept

indicators.note: sheds skin means losing the outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A man called Mick peels after a month of sunburn infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a wound that has gone septic is infected with pus-forming bacteria.

clue.text: Blubber gone bad in freezer

parts.note: to blubber is to cry noisily

indicators.note: gone bad means spoiled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Whale fat that has spoiled is kept in a freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' looks like whale fat but is the verb to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a cryogen is a refrigerant used to produce very low temperatures.

clue.text: Right-wingers in Europe warn M15 about poison

indicators.note: the right wing of a word is its last letter, so take the rightmost letter of each
about means turned round, so the code letters run backwards

parts.note: M15 is read as M, then 1 as ONE and 5 as the Roman V

explanation.surface: Far-right politicians in Europe warn the security service about a poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'M15' looks like MI5, the British security service; read as M, ONE, V, 'about' reverses it to VENOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to envenom is to make poisonous, to inject venom.

clue.text: She was tempted to hoard discarded mobiles etc

indicators.note: to hoard is to store away, so the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A woman was tempted to stockpile old phones.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective term: electronic waste is thrown-away electrical gadgets such as old phones and computers.

clue.text: Extremely chunky bonobo resembling Darth Vader?

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters of each word

explanation.surface: A very chunky ape is compared to the Star Wars villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Example, signalled by the question mark: the Star Wars villain is part man, part machine.

clue.text: Agreed with queen after tense revolutionary period in the past

indicators.note: after places the queen behind the tense letter

parts.note: yes is the word of agreement
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a year is the time the earth takes for one revolution of the sun

explanation.surface: A royal assent given after an anxious revolutionary era long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests political upheaval but means orbiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb use: the word means in former times or bygone days.

clue.text: Separate society that is very English

parts.note: i.e. is id est, that is

explanation.surface: An observation that society keeps itself very English apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to sift or strain, dividing fine material from coarse.

clue.text: They used to get half-cut like this

indicators.note: half-cut means cut in half, keeping the front half of each word

explanation.surface: People once used to get drunk this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for tipsy, but here it halves each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in this way, so, in this manner.

clue.text: Leaders of Conservative revolt are heartless, artful and sly

indicators.note: artful means crafty, so the picked letters are cunningly rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter, so take the first of each

explanation.surface: A Tory rebellion's leaders are callous, crafty and devious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolt' looks like the anagram signal but is just a word giving R; 'artful' rearranges CRAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: arch means knowingly mischievous or cunning.

clue.text: Enormous gong sounds eerie at first

parts.note: a gong is slang for a medal or honour such as the OBE

indicators.note: at first means taking the initial letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: A struck gong produces an eerie sound at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is the British honour Officer of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: very fat, grossly overweight, hence huge in build.

clue.text: Visigoth roughly restraining bear

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A Gothic warrior roughly holds back a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the animal but is the verb to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to endure or undergo something painful.

clue.text: Female relatives chasing last of mouth-watering small pickles

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so these come after the single letter
last of means the final letter of the word

parts.note: her is the female pronoun
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Women of the family pursue a mouth-watering plate of little pickles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small pickles' looks like one phrase; 'small' gives S and 'pickles' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: these are small pickled cucumbers.

clue.text: Nipple rings hurt intermittently, cause of anxiety

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the nipple word goes round the picked letters

parts.note: a teat is a nipple

indicators.note: intermittently means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: Nipple piercings that hurt now and then are worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a threat is a menace, something that causes fear.
